label: bidriware/chemistry/patina-solution
title: The salts of a bidri patina solution
description: Bars of the two salts a thesis dissolved to match the bidri patina, with the one-to-four ratio La Niece and Martin give. Place it beside the blackening step of a bidri page.

u0001.text: The patina forms in a warm solution of one part potassium nitrate to four parts ammonium chloride.

u0002.text: A thesis matched the Bidar fort-soil patina with 20 g of ammonium chloride and 5 g of potassium nitrate in 100 ml of water.

C117.text: La Niece and Martin found that the black patina forms instantly when the alloy is immersed in a warm solution of one part potassium nitrate to four parts ammonium chloride.

quotes.quote: The black patina forms instantaneously on immersion of the alloy in a warm solution of potassium nitrate (one part) and ammonium chloride (four parts).

C131.text: An IIT Madras thesis found that 20 g of ammonium chloride and 5 g of potassium nitrate in 100 ml of water gave a black patina like that from Bidri sand.

quotes.quote: 5g of potassium nitrate (KNO3), 20g of ammonium chloride (NH4Cl) was dissolved in 100 ml of de-ionised water
An alternative to Bidri sand has been identified. A mixture of NH4Cl and KNO3 (20g:5g) in 100mL of de-ionized water renders black patina on the surface similar to one seen with Bidri sand.
